version.changelog:
Version 1.0.6

- Added LICENSE file for clear licensing information.
- Added README.md to provide usage instructions and documentation.

llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed Playwright browser automation tool, but it exposes a local daemon that can run arbitrary code with broad browser and host authority.

dimensions.detail: The daemon listens on `127.0.0.1:19223` without authentication and accepts HTTP GET commands for page actions, page JavaScript evaluation, and Node-side `new Function` execution. Local-only binding helps, but there is no allowlist, sandbox, token, or confirmation gate at the daemon boundary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package has no install scripts in `package.json`, but it pins `playwright` 1.51.0. Public advisories list Playwright versions before 1.55.1 as affected by CVE-2025-59288, with 1.55.1 as patched; the skill partly reduces exposure by preferring system Chrome/Edge and saying no browser download is required. ([github.com](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7mvr-c777-76hp))
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions warn against untrusted snippets and say destructive web actions need user confirmation, but the actual surface is an unrestricted command escape hatch rather than a scoped browser action set.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The daemon is designed to keep browser and page state alive across commands and writes daemon state under `~/.pw-browser`; it can be closed with `close --all`. The persistence is disclosed, but combined with arbitrary code execution it materially increases risk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Browser automation is coherent with the stated purpose, and the artifact discloses screenshots, clicks, forms, tabs, `eval`, `run-code`, downloads, and visible non-headless operation. The concern is that `run-code` turns the skill into arbitrary Playwright/Node execution, which is broader than routine browsing and high-impact if misused.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only in a trusted local session, do not expose the daemon port, avoid running code snippets from web pages or other untrusted sources, close the daemon when finished, and update Playwright to a patched version before relying on it broadly. A sandboxed profile or isolated environment is appropriate for sensitive browsing or account sessions.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The daemon, `eval`, and `run-code` capabilities are explicitly disclosed in `SKILL.md` and `README.md`, so I do not treat this as hidden tool poisoning. The capability breadth is still a Review concern.
[SDI-1] expected: The implementation really exposes `/eval` and `/run-code`; `/run-code` builds a function from caller-supplied text and executes it with the Playwright page object. This is documented, but it is high-impact and insufficiently contained.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Direct Node-side dynamic execution is broader than normal browser automation and has no technical restriction beyond localhost reachability.
[SDI-1] expected: `references/running-code.md` accurately documents arbitrary Playwright code execution, access to page content and storage, downloads, and real form submission, with warnings. The documentation reduces deception concerns but not the authority concern.
[SDI-1] expected: The documented download flow can write to local disk via Playwright download APIs. Downloads are expected for browser automation, but caller-chosen paths through `run-code` should be used only with explicit user direction.
[SC4] unexpected: The pinned Playwright 1.51.0 dependency is below the publicly listed fixed version for CVE-2025-59288, so this is a real supply-chain maintenance issue even though the artifact tries to avoid browser downloads by using system Chrome/Edge. ([github.com](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7mvr-c777-76hp))
